parameters.label: effect-site equilibration rate constant
parameters.covariate_model: ke0 = ln2 / 5.6 min = 0.1238 (Buhrer part II parametric t1/2 ke0, EEG)

extraction.source_locator: Buhrer 1990 part II, text (parametric t1/2 ke0 5.6 min; nonparametric 4.8 min, Table III)

predictive_performance.population: external: post-CABG ICU sedation by TCI, arterial samples, n=63 (reported as MDWR)
external: post-CABG ICU sedation by TCI, arterial samples, n=63 (reported as MDAWR)

extraction.tier_rationale: Small healthy-volunteer study (men aged 33-43). Neither Buhrer paper prints the compartmental parameters; they are printed in Zomorodi 1998 Table 3, and this is the set STANPUMP/CACI used to drive midazolam TCI. Absolute volumes/clearances (no covariates). Weight is required only for per-kg dosing.

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 5.5 via Hypnos)
source_review.method: read a page-image transcription of the primary table (stanpumpR paper digest, checked against the STANPUMP code) and compared each curated value; DOIs CrossRef-verified
sources: https://github.com/StevenLShafer/stanpumpR (papers/digests/PMID_9856717.md: Zomorodi 1998 Table 3 transcribed from the page images, verification 'matches')
https://github.com/StevenLShafer/stanpumpR (R/drugs_midazolam.R: the Buhrer set as entered in STANPUMP; t1/2 ke0 5.6 min from Buhrer part II)
source_review.notes: V1 3.3, V2 17.56, V3 96.76 L and Cl1 0.54, Cl2 2.01, Cl3 0.83 L/min match the digest's Table 3 Buhrer column exactly. The STANPUMP code's unrounded set (0.5352, 2.0145, 0.8321 L/min) rounds to the table. ke0 0.1238/min comes from Buhrer part II's parametric t1/2 ke0 of 5.6 min, as quoted by stanpumpR (part II itself not read here). With these kinetics it peaks at ~3.0 min, against observed EEG peaks of 2.2-2.9 min. HUMAN ITEMS: confirm Table 3 against the primary PDF, and confirm the 5.6 min t1/2 ke0 in Buhrer part II.

notes: The healthy-volunteer half of the midazolam divergence pair. Zomorodi 1998 tested it externally in post-CABG ICU patients and found it nearly unbiased (MDPE -0.39%) while two other published sets (Greenblatt, Maitre) over-predicted the measured concentrations (MDPE -37% and -48%). Its envelope is narrow, so most patients run as a named extrapolation.
